sections.strategy: Tesco relaunched a dedicated F&F clothing website in mid-September with a refreshed design and improved navigation, building on the May 2025 online return. Trade press (Drapers) grouped this alongside George's concept-store push and Tu's collaborations as evidence supermarket fashion is 'stepping up' to compete with high-street chains, with F&F and George now ranking among the UK's top 10 clothing retailers by volume. Tesco's product direction continues toward tighter trend-led edits, fewer repeats of high-volume basics, and more emphasis on responsible sourcing and longevity.
sections.pricing: No new F&F-specific price moves this week, but the competitive backdrop tightened: Primark launched an 'Iconic Value' initiative cutting prices by up to 29% across women's, men's and childrenswear (e.g. cotton-rich jeans to £9, sweatshirts/joggers to £10) in direct response to Shein/Temu pressure. That raises the bar on value perception across the whole supermarket/value fashion tier, including F&F.
sections.launches: F&F added 400 new online-exclusive styles on 17 September spanning essentials, occasionwear and seasonal trend pieces (funnel-neck track jackets, co-ords, leopard-print skirts), with more sizes and improved search. On 18 September, timed to London Fashion Week, F&F ran a pop-up at Frameless Gallery (Marble Arch) showcasing its autumn/winter collection and new brand look; Who What Wear also ran a positive feature on the AW26 range, calling it easy to layer.
sections.gossip: No notable industry gossip or leadership/personnel news surfaced this week.
soWhat: The website relaunch plus 400 new SKUs signals F&F is scaling online assortment breadth — suppliers who can support smaller, faster-turn style drops (rather than large-volume basics runs) are better positioned to win allocation.

Primark's up-to-29% price cuts raise competitive pressure across the value tier; expect Tesco buyers to push harder on landed cost and MOQs on repeat/replenishment lines to protect F&F's price positioning.

The LFW-timed pop-up and 'stepping up' trade narrative (F&F vs George vs Tu) point to continued investment in brand elevation — an opening for vendors who can deliver higher-spec fabric/finish at value-tier cost, especially in outerwear and knitwear categories highlighted in the AW26 collection.
